answer: The gene expression (log2(TPM+1)) distribution across all cell lines is right‑skewed (positive skewness): pooling all 32,017,874 gene × cell‑line values gives Fisher–Pearson sample skewness g1 ≈ 0.69 (0.68971), with the bias‑corrected value identical (G1 = 0.68971) at this sample size. Supporting shape: mean 2.612 > median 2.342, SD 2.505, range [‑2.62, 18.44] with a long right tail (p99 = 9.23, max = 18.44); ~11.1% of values are negative (batch‑correction artifact). Interpretation: a comparatively small set of highly expressed gene/cell‑line combinations pulls the upper tail out, while the majority of values sit near low (near‑zero) expression — the classic signature of heterogeneously expressed protein‑coding genes even after log2(TPM+1) transform. Robustness: the positive sign is not a pooling artifact — skew is positive in 100% of the 1,673 cell lines (per‑cell‑line skew mean 0.69, median 0.68, range 0.27–2.02) and in 65% of the 19,138 genes (per‑gene skew mean 2.46, median 0.41).
